method.cost.p1: Every backtest pays costs. Signals form on a bar’s close and fill at the next open, and A-shares bought today can only be sold tomorrow (T+1). The fee cards and table below are synthetic. In the research the defaults are 5 bp per side for ETFs and 8 bp for single stocks; the cost-sensitivity study found low-turnover trend rules barely affected, while rsi2 breaks even at only 13–24 bp per side.
method.find.bh.b: Every core strategy’s yearly excess return over buy-and-hold was negative, both in and out of sample. What the rules do is make drawdowns shallower: on SPY, for example, blend2’s average yearly worst drawdown was −4.5% against −12.6% for buy-and-hold.
method.find.bh.t: Against buy-and-hold: shallower drawdowns, not higher returns
method.find.dsr.b: 7 core strategies × 12 ETFs × in-sample and out-of-sample gives 168 cells. Without correction, 20 of the 84 out-of-sample cells look significant; once m = 515 trials are counted, none reaches DSR ≥ 0.95, and the best cell scores 0.386. The evidence is too weak to separate these Sharpe ratios from luck, which is not the same as proving the strategies worthless.
method.find.oos.b: Comparing yearly results for 2013–2019 against 2020–2025 gave 84 tests. Only one had a one-sided p below 0.05, fewer than the roughly 4 that chance alone would produce, and it was not significant after Holm correction. With only 7 and 6 years on each side, the test can detect only very large differences, so “not significant” means “cannot tell”, not “no decay”.
method.find.scope: These findings come from the project’s offline research reports on real historical prices, cut off at 31 March 2026. They are research results, not investment advice, and none of them is a recommendation to buy or sell anything.
method.find.t008.b: 485 strategy–parameter combinations on China A-shares were judged by fixed elimination rules. 30 of them (6.2%) passed the monotonicity test, and all 30 then failed the turnover rule. A separate pure-noise simulation shows why 6.2% is not evidence of skill: slow-moving noise factors pass the same test about 5.2% of the time.

method.hero.look_foot: 28 signals · future data truncated and altered
method.lead: A good backtest is not evidence that a strategy works. This page explains how the project tries not to fool itself (in-sample and out-of-sample splits, multiple-testing corrections, costs, survivorship and look-ahead checks) and what that discipline has found so far. Charts and tables here use synthetic demo data; the four key numbers below and the “What the research found” section summarize the project’s own research on real historical data through March 2026.
method.lookahead.p1: A signal may use only data up to the current bar’s close, and fills happen on the next bar. Before 15:30 Beijing time the current day’s bar is off limits, because it covers only half a session.
method.lookahead.p2: This is tested, not assumed. An automated check recomputes every signal with the future deleted, and again with the future randomly altered; past signals must not change by a single digit. Across 7 core strategies and 21 shadow candidates there were 0 violations, and the checker itself was run against deliberately cheating signals to confirm that it catches them.
method.lookahead.p3: Each core strategy also runs on three engines: in-house, Backtrader and RQAlpha. A line-by-line audit found no rule differences across the 7 core strategies and 0 mismatches among 35 comparable parameter defaults. On synthetic prices, target positions differed on at most 0.0806% of days, each case traced to a documented implementation detail such as warm-up length or a floating-point tie.
method.lookahead.title: 5 · No look-ahead, three engines cross-checked
method.neg.p1: Zero survivors is not a failed project; it is the filter doing its job. If the rules let noise through, a few of 485 combinations would pass by luck alone, and it would be tempting to tell a story about them. A process that can say “nothing here” is one whose “something here” will mean more.
method.neg.p2: The result is also protected against second attempts. Each verdict is written to a write-once trial log and frozen; re-running the same strategy and parameters with different inputs returns the frozen verdict, not another chance to pass. Any new idea has to be run as a new experiment, and its trials are added to the count used in the multiple-testing correction.
method.neg.p3: We are equally careful not to overstate it. The verdict rests on a single replay over a short training window. Two robustness variants reused the frozen verdicts, so their agreement is not independent confirmation. And in simulation the monotonicity test recognizes a weak but real signal (IC = 0.02) only about 52% of the time, so zero survivors does not prove these strategies carry no information.
method.neg.title: 7 · Why a negative result is worth publishing
method.of.p1: Try enough parameter sets and one will look good by chance. The Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) raises the bar from “Sharpe above zero” to “Sharpe above the best you would expect from pure noise after m trials”, adjusting for sample length, skew and fat tails. The figures in the cards below are a synthetic example.
method.of.p2: In the research, trials are counted honestly: m = 515 (7 core strategies, 18 shadow candidates and 490 trials from the T008 replay), and a result passes only with DSR ≥ 0.95. For scale: after 515 trials, the best of a set of pure-noise strategies has an annualized Sharpe of about 1.16 on average. PBO, the probability that the in-sample winner falls below the median out of sample, is shown here only as a demo metric.
method.of.title: 2 · Multiple testing and overfitting
method.sb.p1: Backtesting only on stocks that still exist today means knowing in advance who survived, which flatters the results. The ideal universe is built as it stood at the time, with delisted names kept until their last trading day. The table below is a synthetic illustration of how large the effect can be.
method.sb.p2: An honest limitation: the project’s current A-share data does not yet include delisted stocks. Single-stock results in the research are therefore biased upward, and estimates of the cost of being unable to sell (limit-down days, suspensions) are only lower bounds.
method.wf.p1: Parameters are chosen on one stretch of history and judged on the stretch that follows, which the selection step never sees. Below is a synthetic five-fold example: each fold trains on 46 months and tests on the next 12, and the five test windows together form an out-of-sample record you could actually have had at the time.
method.wf.p2: The project’s research uses a fixed split: 2013–2019 in-sample, 2020 to March 2026 out-of-sample, with prices cut at 31 March 2026 before any signal is computed. One caveat up front: the later window has been displayed and discussed many times, and the strategy list itself was settled after seeing it, so it is really a second in-sample period. A clean test needs rules registered in advance and data that arrives afterwards.

replay.lead: Each strategy is replayed day by day as if it were live, using only the data available at the time, to see when it wins and when it loses. This leaderboard is synthetic; in the real T008 replay, no strategy–parameter combination survived the elimination rules.

story.hero.sub: Three independent backtest engines, strict next-bar fills, a fixed in-sample / out-of-sample split and corrections for multiple testing. The most informative result so far is a negative one.
story.s2.sub: Trend, breakout, mean-reversion, momentum and factor rules, each written out explicitly with default parameters. The ranking below is synthetic: a high Sharpe is where the questions start, not where they end.

story.s3.sub: Each core strategy is implemented three times: in-house, in Backtrader and in RQAlpha. A rule-by-rule audit of the 7 core strategies found no rule differences, and the 7 implementation-level gaps it did find are documented rather than hidden.
story.s3.title: Three engines, one set of rules.
story.s4.sub: Parameters are chosen on earlier data and judged on later data. In the research, 2013–2019 is in-sample and 2020 through March 2026 is out-of-sample, although the later window has been looked at often enough that we treat it as a second in-sample period.
story.s4.title: Time only runs forward.
